How does this occupation differ from electrical and electronics installers and repairers and electrical engineers?

Electricians install and maintain power, communication, lighting, and control systems in homes, commercial premises, and factories; the installers-and-repairers group also covers five equipment specialisms. Electrical engineers research, design, develop, and test, and may supervise implementation; the fact that they usually do not personally perform repairs is not an absolute boundary.

Work context
Electricians install, test, and repair electrical wiring, equipment, and fixtures at construction sites, factories, and facilities, applying safety measures according to codes and work permits.
Work locations: construction sites, factories, facilities, and existing buildings, varying by project.
Main work objects: electrical wiring, distribution equipment, lighting and control equipment, and grounding systems.
Handoffs are required with project teams, other trades, property management, and suppliers.
Working hours: mostly full time, with more overtime around deadlines and maintenance windows; emergency repairs require readiness to respond at any time.
Risks mainly arise from live electrical work, work at height, lifting and carrying, and tool injuries.
Tools and information: hand and power tools, instruments such as multimeters and clamp meters, drawings and code documents, work permits, and recording systems.

Structured explanation of the occupational profile
O*NET47-2111 Electricians: 21 tasks, RC, Zone3; installation, maintenance, and repair of power, communication, lighting, and control systems in homes, commercial premises, and factories.
BLS OES / O*NET: nationwide median annual wage of USD 63,190 in 2025 (median hourly wage USD 30.38); five percentile figures: USD 42,640 / 49,430 / 63,190 / 83,940 / 108,510.

O*NET education responses: 62% postsecondary certificate, 31% high school, 2% below high school; Zone3 describes preparation level. BLS describes a typical apprenticeship of 4–5 years; generic Zone examples do not replace the occupation-specific duration.

Similar roles in mainland China mainly involve building electrical installation, equipment maintenance, and repair. Entrants often start in construction or repair roles and obtain certificates as locally required; these do not correspond one-to-one to this U.S. occupation. Employment in 2025: 821,000; growth of 9% from 2025 to 2035; average annual openings 72,700, including replacement needs. In 2025: electrical contractors and other wiring installation contractors 66%, self-employed 7%, manufacturing 6%, government 3%, employment services 2%.

Occupational boundaries: this page follows U.S. O*NET-SOC 47-2111.00, "Electricians": roles installing, maintaining, and repairing electrical wiring, equipment, and fixtures and ensuring work complies with relevant codes. paragraphs: Electrical and electronics installers and repairers
Install and repair electrical and electronic equipment, including commercial and industrial equipment, transport equipment, power facilities, and avionics.
Their focus is mainly equipment itself in industrial, transport, and power settings; this occupation mainly concerns electrical wiring systems in buildings and facilities.
Choose that occupation for industrial and transport equipment repair; choose this occupation for wiring installation in buildings and facilities.
Electrical and electronics engineering technologists and technicians
Provide design support, assembly and testing, maintenance, and troubleshooting under engineering personnel's direction.
Handle test records and engineering support, usually without performing on-site wiring and installation.
Choose that occupation if you want testing and engineering support and are willing to work under engineers' direction; choose this occupation for frontline installation and repair.
Electrical engineers
Handle design calculations, compliance conclusions, and document signing, usually without personally wiring or repairing.
Choose that occupation if you are willing to study theory over the long term and take design responsibility; choose this occupation if you prefer hands-on site work.
Heating, air conditioning, and refrigeration mechanics and installers
The focus is HVAC and refrigeration equipment and piping; electrical work is limited to equipment controls and power-supply interfaces.
Choose that occupation if mechanical and refrigeration systems interest you more; choose this occupation if electrical systems themselves interest you more.
Industrial machinery mechanics
The focus is mechanical, hydraulic, and pneumatic systems; electrical work centres on equipment control circuits.
Choose that occupation if you prefer maintaining machinery and equipment itself; choose this occupation if you prefer electrical systems in buildings and facilities.
Security and fire alarm systems installers
The focus is specialized alarm and fire-protection equipment and associated codes.
Choose that occupation if specialized fire-protection and security codes interest you more; choose this occupation for general electrical installation and repair.
How to distinguish adjacent occupations

These occupations all involve electrical or electromechanical equipment, but differ in work objects, codes, and entry requirements; use them to check your direction rather than treating them as interchangeable.

Adjacent paths differ in work objects (electrical systems in buildings and facilities, equipment itself, or design documents), code systems, and entry requirements (apprenticeships and licences, engineering degrees, or professional qualifications). How AI may change electricians' work

AI and digital tools can help consult electrical codes and product information, organize quantities and material lists, and read and organize test records. They cannot replace on-site verification of absence of voltage and circuit verification, root-cause judgement, work to code, or work permits, and do not bear safety or compliance responsibility. entries.answer: Install, maintain, and repair electrical wiring, equipment, and fixtures: follow drawings and codes to install conduit, pull wires, make connections, and secure equipment; de-energize, verify absence of voltage, and test; troubleshoot faults; energize according to procedure and hand over work records.
entries.question: What do electricians mainly do?

entries.answer: This occupation mainly installs and repairs electrical wiring, equipment, and fixtures in buildings and facilities, following building electrical codes, licensing, and work permits. Equipment installers and repairers mainly repair equipment itself in industrial, transport, and power facilities; electrical engineers handle design calculations, compliance conclusions, and signing design documents.
